walk.title: Solve it: Harvest Lane's first three automations
walk.sample: One week of Tolu's admin diary · 270 orders a week · 9 admin steps

steps.say: Tolu spends almost four hours a day moving information around. Before we touch any tool, we find out which parts a machine should take.
show: 45 orders a day · 6 days a week

steps.say: We start with a week of real data. Tolu writes down every admin step, how often it happens and how long it takes, because a measured week beats a guess.
show: Step · runs per week · minutes per run

steps.say: Now we score each row. Runs times minutes gives the time; the error factor makes costly mistakes count more.
Then we divide by difficulty, never multiply, so hard tasks drop down the list. Keep every row in per-week units.
Sort by priority. Copying orders into the notebook leads at 540, then the total and the payment check at 270 each.
Notice reading the WhatsApp order scores lowest, at 45. Keep an eye on it, because the next step pulls it back in.
The ranking says automate copying first, but copying needs the order in a clean shape, and reading messy WhatsApp text is hard. So we check what depends on what.
Here's the key move: change the input, not just the steps. A short order form makes the order arrive already structured, and steps one to four collapse into one automation.
show: Input: order form or WhatsApp menu

steps.say: We choose three. Order capture first, then payment confirmation from a payment link, then a stock update that rides on the clean order data.
Route planning stays with a person on purpose. It happens six times a week and needs local judgment.
show: Later quick wins: thank-you, weekly summary

steps.say: Last, the payback. Eighteen hours saved a week, worth about one hundred and ninety-three thousand naira a month if Tolu's hour is worth two thousand five hundred.
show: Saved: 1,080 of 1,358 min a week ≈ 18 h

walk.end: Measured pain, scored honestly, dependencies checked: that's how you pick what to automate. Now score five tasks of your own.
